analyst_view.overall: Early view: a one-off Eastern Conference Wild Card, No. 8 Orlando against No. 9 Cincinnati, with a draw after 90 minutes going straight to penalties and the winner meeting Supporters' Shield winners Nashville in a best-of-three. Orlando lean on Antoine Griezmann (14 goals and 8 assists in 18 games, October/November Player of the Month) but have Robin Jansson out after foot surgery, Tyrese Spicer out with a foot injury at the last check, and six players away this week, including Braian Ojeda in Japan on 17 November and Maxime Crepeau and Justin Ellis playing on 16 and 17 November. Cincinnati have conceded 75 goals, are short at centre-back (Hagglund concussion, Malatini leg, Hadebe off injured against Nashville), and Kevin Denkey plays for Togo in Lome on 17 November; the season series was a 6-2 Cincinnati win in May and a 1-1 draw in Orlando in August with Griezmann playing.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.9 goals, built on two defences that leak: Cincinnati conceded 75, the third-most in MLS, and the August meeting in Orlando still ended only 1-1. I lean a little lower because a single knockout game with no extra time usually starts cagey, Orlando's last two games produced five goals in total (0-4 at Charlotte, 1-0 against New England), and Orlando lose Spicer's pace while Denkey and Ojeda arrive back from long trips two days before kick-off. Over 2.5 still looks right; four or more needs an early goal to open it up.

corners.text: The site expects 10.1 corners, split almost evenly. Cincinnati's 3-4-1-2 pushes both wing-backs high and Orlando will attack the space behind them, which fits a normal count rather than a big swing either way. Nothing in this week's news moves it, so I stay with the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards and lean under 4.5, but I lean higher. Cincinnati picked up five yellows in the Decision Day loss to Nashville (Nwobodo, Evander, Gidi, Smith and Bucha), Evander and Miazga were both booked in the August draw in Orlando, and Crepeau was booked for time wasting against New England. Win-or-go-home stakes, tired legs after the international break and a likely chase late on add to it.

shots.text: The site expects 29 shots, which is a lot for a knockout game. I lean lower: Orlando are without Spicer and will have several players back from national-team trips only a day or two before, and Cincinnati's patched-up centre-back group may make Pat Noonan less willing to throw both wing-backs forward from the start.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.6 shots on target. I lean lower, in line with the goals: Orlando scored once in their last two games, and I expect fewer clear chances in a tight one-off game with travel-weary players on both sides. Griezmann, Denkey and Evander can still test Crepeau and Roman Celentano, so around nine looks fair.
